summary: Round r1 (restricted network). Q1 (how Fed and RBI policy rates transmit to Nepal's interest rates and liquidity) is answered only at the level of research design; all empirical items are pending. Primary leads located: the latest FOMC statement (16 September 2026), its implementation note and Summary of Economic Projections, H.15; the RBI MPC resolution and minutes for August 2026 and the June 2026 Monetary Policy Statement, DBIE; the NRB Monetary Policy archive (FY2026/27 document not yet located as a direct file), the FY2025/26 Monetary Policy and its mid-term review, the August 2026 CME release with interbank-rate tables, and NRB research on pass-through, the bank-lending channel, Indian monetary spillovers and interbank volatility. Working hypothesis (assumption, untested): the RBI channel runs mainly via the peg and INR/USD, the Fed channel mainly via INR/USD, remittance-source economies and USD debt service; domestic liquidity (remittances, government balances) is expected to dominate NRB interbank rates. Search-surfaced secondary reports were internally inconsistent on the FY2026/27 NRB policy-rate level, so only the NRB document can be used.

findings.note: Fed statements 2026 (latest located: 16 September 2026), H.15 monthly effective federal funds rate; calendar basis, re-aggregate monthly to Nepal FY.

findings.note: RBI MPC resolutions June 2026 and August 2026; DBIE repo and weighted average call rate monthly; Indian FY April-March to be converted to Nepal FY via monthly data.

findings.claim: Q1: NRB policy rate and corridor (SDF floor, SLF/bank-rate ceiling) for FY2026/27 and history since FY2016/17.
findings.note: NRB Monetary Policy FY2026/27 document (direct PDF not located; archive lead given) plus each annual MP and mid-term review. Secondary news items surfaced in search gave mutually inconsistent descriptions of the FY2026/27 policy-rate level; the value must come from the NRB document itself.

findings.note: CME monthly tables (latest located: August 2026 release, first month of FY2026/27) and historical CME annual statistical tables; mid-month Nepali calendar basis.

findings.claim: Q1: Empirical pass-through from Fed and RBI rates to NRB interbank, T-bill, deposit and lending rates.
findings.note: Extract estimates and methods from NRB WP 61, Interest Rate Pass-Through in Nepal, Indian monetary policy spillover article, WP 49; record each estimate as an observation with its sample period and method. No coefficient is reported here.

findings.claim: Transmission design: under the NPR-INR peg with an open current account towards India, the working hypothesis is that Indian policy rates affect Nepal mainly through (i) the peg and INR/USD, (ii) relative returns influencing informal and formal cross-border flows, and (iii) Indian demand; the Fed affects Nepal mainly indirectly via INR/USD, Gulf/Malaysia labour demand and remittances, and USD-denominated debt service rather than through direct capital-account arbitrage, given Nepal's capital controls. To be tested against the pass-through literature above.

Nepal's domestic interest rates are expected to be dominated by domestic liquidity (remittance inflows, government cash balances at NRB, credit demand) in the short run; external rate signals are a secondary, lagged channel. This must be tested (e.g. interbank rate regressed on liquidity indicators and RBI rate changes) before use in the model.

Model entry: foreign policy rates enter the shared model only as exogenous monthly paths re-aggregated to Nepal FY averages; no rate path is a forecast. Scenario paths (S04, S10) will be stated as labelled assumptions anchored on the latest dated primary decision.

data_gaps: Direct PDF of NRB Monetary Policy for FY2026/27 (2083/84) not located; need its corridor table (policy rate, SDF rate, SLF/bank rate), CRR/SLR and targets.
Monthly NRB weighted average interbank rate series FY2016/17-FY2026/27 in machine-readable form (CME tables or NRB database) not located as a single file.
RBI DBIE extraction format (series codes for repo rate and weighted average call money rate) to be confirmed on access.
No located study estimates a direct Fed-to-Nepal interest-rate pass-through; this may need an original estimate (labelled `estimate` with method) in r2.
The session web-search budget was exhausted before all planned searches ran; some leads below were reused from 16A/16B and some document-level leads remain unlocated (listed individually).
No lead URL was downloaded in r1 (data hosts blocked); all values await `python -m src.cli leads --fetch`, extraction and ingest in r2.

assumptions.text: Monthly foreign rate series are averaged over Nepal FY months (mid-July to mid-July) using day-weighting; the Nepali-calendar mid-month boundaries are approximated by Gregorian mid-month and the approximation is documented.
Policy-rate paths for scenarios are stress settings, not forecasts; the FOMC SEP median is recorded as an FOMC participant projection (observation), never as a platform forecast.
Transmission hypothesis (peg/INR channel for RBI; indirect channels for Fed) is a research hypothesis to be tested, not a finding.

challenges.text: Agent 03 should not treat NRB interbank rates as driven by foreign policy rates without a tested link; domestic liquidity (remittance inflows, government deposits at NRB) should be modelled first, with external rates as an exogenous secondary channel.

X20 (global and Indian interest rates) is assigned to 20A with no exposure-register id; suggest linking it to EXP-10 (NPR-INR peg) and EXP-11 (external debt) because the Fed channel runs through USD debt service and INR/USD.

Watch item: secondary reports disagree about the NRB FY2026/27 policy-rate level; not an inter-source conflict yet because no primary value has been retrieved. Resolve from the NRB Monetary Policy FY2026/27 document before any use.

uncertainty: High. No rate has been retrieved; the transmission mechanism is stated as an untested hypothesis. The NRB FY2026/27 policy document has not been located as a direct file. Existing NRB pass-through studies cover different samples and methods and may not capture the post-2017 corridor regime or recent regime changes. External rates are calendar/Indian-FY monthly series and require documented conversion to Nepal FY.

rate_transmission_evidence.question: How do Fed and RBI policy rates transmit to Nepal's interest rates and liquidity?

literature_evidence.method: Extract estimated pass-through coefficients, lags, samples and identification from each study; record as observations (source_id academic/nrb) with study metadata; do not pool across methods.

channels_hypothesised.channel: RBI rate -> INR/USD and Indian demand -> Nepal prices and trade (via NPR-INR peg)
RBI/Indian money-market rates -> relative returns -> cross-border (incl. informal) flows -> NRB liquidity
Fed rate -> USD strength/INR/USD -> NPR/USD -> import prices and USD debt service
Fed/global rates -> Gulf and Malaysia activity -> remittances -> NRB liquidity and interbank rate
Domestic: remittance inflows and government balances at NRB -> interbank rate within corridor

rate_transmission_evidence.planned_method: r2: (1) build monthly panel FY2016/17-FY2026/27 of Fed, RBI, India call, NRB corridor and interbank rates plus NRB liquidity and remittance series; (2) event study around RBI and Fed decisions; (3) local projections of NRB interbank and lending rates on RBI and Fed changes controlling for domestic liquidity; (4) compare with published NRB estimates; label outputs `estimate` with method.

parameters: external_rate_path_usd (calendar monthly, converted to Nepal FY)

rate_transmission_evidence.fiscal_year_note: Fed series calendar; RBI decisions dated, Indian data April-March; NRB Nepal FY mid-July to mid-July with Nepali-calendar mid-month dates.
